items.title: Ray Blue interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 23, 2022
items.q: I was fortunate to interview Phil Woods

ctx.x: Somewhat. Well not where I was going to end up, but how I get here. Here’s how it went: I was offered music scholarships out of high school. But there was something — I didn’t take them because there was other things I wanted to learn you know. And I said — and that’s how I you know, that’s how I thought about it. So yeah, so I studied soc and psych and then grad school I went into clinical social work. And when I got to grad school that’s when I actually really started to bear down and started studying saxophone…

Now when I read that I got this flashback to I was fortunate to interview Phil Woods and he said, well a jazz career, let me put it this way, if you’re trying to decide between a career as a brain surgeon or a jazz tenor man — he literally said ‘tenor man’ — he goes be the brain surgeon.

Yeah. That’s what some people would say. I know people that said he gave up music to make a living. You know? But you know one of the things my mentor in grad school, and I believe all the things we learn in life are transferrable to any situation you know. She
